note.note:
Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- Vincent (DOB 09-May-2016) presents with 1-week sore throat progressing to dry cough, mild exertional dyspnea, intermittent wheeze and chest discomfort; presentation most consistent with an acute viral upper-respiratory infection/viral bronchitis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sore throat began last Thu/Fri → dry, non-productive cough after 1-2 days → exertional shortness of breath, occasional wheeze & mild chest pain after further 1-2 days.  
• Course: Fluctuating; subjective fever first 3 days (now resolved); intermittent headaches; reduced appetite; no weight loss.  
• Pertinent negatives: No sputum, hemoptysis, nasal congestion, sinus symptoms, night-time worsening, rashes, or recent long-haul travel.  
• Past medical history: None reported; no asthma or thromboembolic history.  
• Medications: None.  
• Allergies: Peanuts (no drug allergies).  
• Family history: Mother—lung cancer; no clotting disorders.  
• Social / preventive: Non-smoker (minimal past experimentation); no known asbestos exposure; lives in UK >12 yrs; recent travel only within Europe; exercises regularly; off work 2 days this week and requests sick note.

Examination:
• Remote consult; no vitals available.  
• Patient feels no cervical lymphadenopathy; throat visualization not performed.  
• No objective respiratory exam performed.

Impression:
1. Acute viral upper-respiratory infection / viral bronchitis – most likely given classic sequence (sore throat → dry cough, low-grade fever) and gradual improvement.  
2. COVID-19 infection – moderate likelihood; symptom overlap (sore throat, dry cough, fever, headache, appetite loss); advise testing if available.  
3. Reactive airway disease/new-onset asthma – consider if wheeze or dyspnea persist after viral illness resolves.

Plan:
• Symptomatic treatment: Paracetamol for pain/fever, adequate fluids, rest.  
• Issued sick note for additional days off work.  
• Safety-net advice: Seek in-person medical review (GP or emergency) if breathlessness worsens, new or severe chest pain, persistent fever, hemoptysis, or no improvement within 4–5 days.  
• Monitor symptoms; if still symptomatic or COVID suspected, arrange local COVID-19 testing per public health guidance.  
• No antibiotics or other prescriptions indicated at present.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements: Objective vitals (temperature, pulse, SpO₂, BP), physical exam findings, current immunization/COVID test status, occupation details, full medication/allergy reconciliation.  
● Transcript–DDx conflicts: None significant noted.  
● Transcript quality: Acceptable but occasional inaudible/over-talk; patient DOB likely misstated (appears adult).
